entities.summary:
Luli or Elulaios was a Phoenician king of the city of Tyre from approximately 700 to 694 BCE. During his reign, Tyre lost what remained of its power to Assyria.

As one of the last major Phoenician cities before the Assyrian conquest, Luli's rule marked the beginning of the end for Tyre's independence and influence in the Mediterranean region. His failure to resist the growing Assyrian empire had significant consequences for the balance of power in the ancient Near East.

The legacy of Luli can be seen in the subsequent history of Tyre, which was eventually absorbed into the Neo-Babylonian Empire and later became a major center of Hellenistic culture. Despite its decline, Tyre's maritime trade and cultural exchange continued to shape the region for centuries to come.

Luli's story serves as a reminder of the fragile nature of power in ancient civilizations, where even the most seemingly strong empires can be toppled by a combination of internal weaknesses and external pressures.
